traceability.notes:
This file is a concrete development story/specification, not a planning-only document, so it is in scope for implementation assessment.
All acceptance criteria and detailed requirements for 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS are satisfied with concrete, passing tests: - Core Functionality & REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION / REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED: The two rules require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation are implemented as ESLint rules over the same set of function-like constructs (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature), explicitly excluding arrow functions by default. Tests show valid and invalid cases for each construct and confirm arrow functions are not required by default, but can be annotated. - Quality Standards: Helpers, rule meta, and context.report usage are thoroughly covered by unit tests and follow ESLint best practices (structured messageIds, correct node locations, fixers, and suggest entries). The rules are integrated into the plugin with proper configs (validated in other suites) and have robust helper layers. - Integration & REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT: TypeScript syntax (TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature, TS FunctionExpression in variable declarators, including exported forms) is fully supported, as demonstrated by multiple passing tests tagged [REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT]. This ensures compatibility with JS, TS, and mixed codebases. - User Experience & REQ-ERROR-LOCATION: Tests for core helpers show that violations are reported at the function name or closest relevant node, and error messages are specific about missing annotation types. Additional tests (e.g., error-reporting enhancements in a related story) validate that messaging is clear and actionable. - Error Handling: Edge-case tests for IO and helper functions demonstrate that malformed or missing JSDoc/comments, missing sourceCode, malformed ranges/locations, and thrown errors from getText/getSourceCode are handled gracefully without crashing, returning safe fallbacks instead. - Configurability (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY): Both rules support the same scope and exportPriority semantics, and this behavior is verified by dedicated tests, ensuring exported vs non-exported prioritization and scoped enforcement are consistent across both rules. - Documentation: Rule docs for both rules exist and describe behavior, supported constructs, and configuration options, including scope and exportPriority.
The story’s Definition of Done includes some broader project-level items (e.g., integration into presets, performance testing with large codebases) that are partially addressed by other stories and performance/integration test suites. For this specific story’s own acceptance criteria and technical requirements, the implementation is complete and verified by passing tests. Therefore, the status is PASSED.
